topic_title: Thanksgiving Window Painting: 9 Easy Designs That Wipe Off
intro: Window painting for Thanksgiving works best with simple, bold shapes that read from across a room or the street: leaves, pumpkins, a turkey, a few words. Before you start, decide whether the design is for inside or outside the glass, since paint on the outside faces rain and cold. Liquid chalk markers and washable window markers are easier to control than brushes, and a design drawn with dry-erase marker on the opposite side of the glass gives you a guide to trace. Test any product on a small corner first.

picks.description: A border of falling leaves around the edges of the glass is the easiest Thanksgiving window design to get right, because leaves look natural when they are uneven. Draw maple, oak and simple oval leaves in orange, red, yellow and brown, clustering more in the top corners and letting a few drift down the sides. Outline each leaf first with a chalk marker, fill it in, then add a single center vein and a short stem in a darker shade. A border leaves the middle of the window clear, so the room keeps its light and you can add lettering later. It takes roughly an hour for a standard window. The trade-off is repetition: leaves all the same size and color look flat, so vary both deliberately.
picks.best_for: Beginners and kids who want a design that forgives mistakes
picks.skip_if: You want one bold central picture rather than an edge pattern
picks.quirky_fact: Overlapping two leaves slightly makes a border look fuller without drawing any extra shapes.
picks.product_name: Chalkola Liquid Chalk Markers, 10 Pack, Fall Colors

picks.breed: Pumpkin Trio on the Sill Line
picks.description: Three pumpkins of different sizes along the bottom of the window give the design a base, as if they are sitting on the sill. Draw each pumpkin as a set of overlapping curved sections, with the center section largest, then add a brown stem, a curling green vine and a leaf or two. Use orange for the main pumpkin and try one white or pale green pumpkin for contrast. Fill with color, then add darker orange lines between the sections for shape. Pumpkins are easy enough for children to draw and still read clearly from the street. The trade-off is that pumpkins also say Halloween, so pair them with leaves, wheat or Give Thanks lettering to make the Thanksgiving theme obvious.
picks.best_for: Pairing with lettering or leaves above to complete the window
picks.skip_if: You have already painted pumpkins for Halloween and want something new
picks.quirky_fact: Drawing the pumpkin's center section first, then the sides behind it, makes the shape look rounder.

picks.description: A short phrase such as Give Thanks, Grateful or Happy Thanksgiving in the center of the window tells everyone the theme at a glance. Write it in a simple script or bold capitals with a white or cream chalk marker, which shows up on glass better than dark colors. Lightly sketch the letters first with a dry-erase marker so you can adjust spacing before committing. If the lettering faces the street, write it in reverse on the inside of the glass, or tape a mirrored printout to the outside and trace it. Add a few leaves or a wheat sprig around the words. The trade-off is that uneven lettering is more noticeable than uneven leaves, so practice the phrase on paper once before starting.
picks.best_for: Storefronts, front doors and classroom windows facing a hallway
picks.skip_if: You are painting with young kids who cannot write yet
picks.quirky_fact: Thicker downstrokes and thinner upstrokes are what make simple marker lettering look like calligraphy.
picks.product_name: Uni Chalk Marker PWE-5M, White, Medium Bullet Tip

picks.description: A round cartoon turkey is the classic Thanksgiving window picture, and it is easier than it looks: a brown circle for the body, a smaller circle on top for the head, and a fan of colorful tail feathers behind. Paint the feathers as long rounded shapes in red, orange, yellow and brown, then add an orange beak, a red wattle, two eyes and simple stick feet. Children can each paint one feather, which makes it a good group project for families or classrooms. Placing the turkey in a lower corner leaves room for lettering above. It takes about 30 to 45 minutes. The trade-off is scale: a turkey smaller than about a foot across loses its detail from outside, so draw it large.
picks.best_for: Classrooms and families painting together with young children
picks.skip_if: You prefer an elegant, grown-up look over a playful one
picks.quirky_fact: A real turkey's tail can fan out into a semicircle of around 18 feathers when the bird displays.

picks.description: A cluster of three to five sunflowers growing up from a bottom corner adds warm color without the cartoon feel of a turkey. Paint each flower as a dark brown center surrounded by a ring of pointed yellow petals, then add a second, slightly offset ring in orange or gold for depth. Long green stems and broad leaves give the cluster height. Sunflowers look good on narrow windows, sidelights and glass doors where a wide design will not fit. Dot the centers with a lighter brown for texture. The trade-off is that sunflowers read as late summer as much as Thanksgiving, so add a few falling leaves or a small pumpkin nearby to tie them to the season.
picks.best_for: Narrow windows, sidelights and glass doors
picks.skip_if: You want a design that says Thanksgiving with no other elements
picks.quirky_fact: A sunflower head is made of hundreds of tiny florets arranged in interlocking spirals.
picks.product_name: Chalkola Liquid Chalk Markers, 6mm Reversible Tip, 8 Pack

picks.description: A painted garland of acorns and oak leaves swagged across the top of the window works like a fabric valance and frames the view. Draw a gentle drooping line from corner to corner, then add oak leaves along it with acorns hanging in pairs between them. Acorns are simple: an oval nut in tan or brown with a textured cap drawn as a dome with crosshatched lines. Keep the garland to the top quarter of the glass so it does not block much light. It pairs well with lettering below or a pumpkin trio at the bottom. The trade-off is that a long garland takes patience, often an hour or more on a wide window, and works best painted by one person for a consistent look.
picks.best_for: Wide picture windows that need a frame rather than a centerpiece
picks.skip_if: You want a quick project finished in under half an hour
picks.quirky_fact: Oak trees often produce far more acorns in some years than others, which naturalists call a mast year.
picks.product_name: Posca PC-5M Paint Marker Set, 8 Colors

picks.description: A cornucopia, the curved horn-shaped basket spilling fruit and vegetables, is a traditional Thanksgiving symbol and a satisfying centerpiece for a large window. Draw the horn in tan with crosshatched basket lines, curving to a point at one end and opening wide at the other. Fill the opening with simple shapes: round apples, a bunch of purple grapes, small pumpkins, ears of corn and a few leaves. It is the most detailed design on this list and suits older kids or adults who enjoy drawing. Use a printed outline traced from the other side of the glass if freehand feels daunting. The trade-off is time and space: it needs a window at least two feet wide and an hour or two of work.
picks.best_for: Large front windows and adults who enjoy a detailed project
picks.skip_if: You are short on time or painting with very young children
picks.quirky_fact: The cornucopia, or horn of plenty, dates back to ancient Greek and Roman art as a symbol of abundance.
picks.product_name: Reusable Fall Harvest Stencils for Painting, Plastic Template Set

picks.description: A single oversized slice of pumpkin pie with a swirl of whipped cream is a cheerful, food-themed design that suits kitchen windows, bakeries and cafes. Draw a wedge shape in orange with a thick golden-brown crust along the back edge, then a white cloud of whipped cream on top. A darker orange line just inside the outline gives the filling depth. Add a fork, a few steam curls or small leaves around it. It is simple enough for children and quick to finish, often in about 20 minutes. The trade-off is that a lone pie slice can look sparse on a big window, so either draw it large or pair it with lettering such as Pie Season or Give Thanks.
picks.best_for: Kitchen windows, cafes and bakeries wanting a playful design
picks.skip_if: You want a design that works for a formal entryway
picks.quirky_fact: Canned pumpkin for pies is often made from varieties of winter squash related to butternut rather than carving pumpkins.

picks.description: A smiling scarecrow with a straw hat, patched shirt and straw poking from the sleeves brings a farm-harvest look to the window. Build it from simple shapes: a round tan face, a triangle hat, a rectangle shirt in plaid and short straw strokes in yellow at the wrists and neck. Add a crow perched on one arm for a story element kids enjoy. Place the scarecrow off to one side so leaves or lettering fill the rest of the glass. It suits classroom windows and front windows facing a family street. The trade-off is that faces are easy to get wrong, so keep the expression simple: two dots for eyes, a stitched line for a smile and a triangle nose.
picks.best_for: Classroom and family windows wanting a playful harvest scene
picks.skip_if: You prefer a minimal design with only leaves and words
picks.quirky_fact: Farmers have used human-shaped figures to scare birds from crops for thousands of years, in many cultures.
picks.product_name: Chalkola Liquid Chalk Markers, Fine Tip, 12 Pack

faqs.question: What paint is best for Thanksgiving window painting?
faqs.answer: Liquid chalk markers and washable window markers are the easiest choices because they draw like pens and wipe off with a damp cloth. For larger areas, many people use washable tempera paint mixed with a small squeeze of dish soap, which helps it come off glass later. Avoid acrylic craft paint on windows unless you are ready to scrape it off with a razor blade.

faqs.question: How do you get window paint off glass?
faqs.answer: Most chalk markers and washable window paints come off with warm water and a microfiber cloth or a squeegee. Spray the design, wait a minute so the paint softens, then wipe. Stubborn spots usually lift with glass cleaner or a little vinegar in water. Check the product label, since some chalk markers can stain porous or etched glass, and test a corner first.

faqs.question: Should I paint on the inside or outside of the window?
faqs.answer: Paint on the inside when the design is mainly for your home or classroom, or when the weather is wet or below freezing, since rain and frost spoil outdoor paint. Paint on the outside if you want people walking past to see crisp lines without reflections. Writing must be drawn in reverse on the inside to read correctly from the street.

faqs.question: How do I draw a window design if I can't draw?
faqs.answer: Print a simple outline, such as a leaf, pumpkin or turkey, and tape it to the outside of the glass facing in. Trace it from the inside with a light chalk marker, then fill in the color. Reusable plastic stencils work the same way. Basic shapes repeated several times, like a row of leaves, look finished even without drawing skill.

faqs.question: Is window painting a good Thanksgiving activity for kids?
faqs.answer: Yes, with washable window markers it is low-mess and easy to fix, since mistakes wipe away with a damp cloth. Give younger children the lower panes and simple shapes like leaves or pumpkins, and keep an adult on the ladder for anything higher up. Lay a towel on the sill to catch drips, and choose markers labeled non-toxic and washable.

seo_title: Thanksgiving Window Painting: 9 Easy Designs for 2026
answer: Start with a falling leaves border, add a pumpkin trio along the bottom of the glass, and finish with Give Thanks lettering in the center. The deciding factor is the paint: liquid chalk markers or washable window markers wipe off with water, so you can repaint freely and clean up in minutes.
